candidates.explanation: Labels behavior is coherently colocated under one module with route-private UI in app. It avoids speculative ports/application operations, uses direct RSC reads, GET browser reads, and top-level Server Actions, derives identity server-side with scoped queries and RLS, and privately maps provider rows. No negative rubric item is violated.

The feature and route glue are placed appropriately, all three channels are correct, authorization is enforced server-side with RLS, and row mapping is private. However, the service-plus-repository structure adds an avoidable forwarding CRUD layer despite the fixed provider, and generic lib buckets are proposed.

The proposal correctly avoids a repository port/application use-case layer and has sound channel, authentication, authorization, mapping, and client/server separation. It does not colocate behavior under one labels root, instead scattering it across domain, data, adapters, client-cache, and UI; its per-operation inbound wrappers also violate the wrapper penalty.

The runtime channels, server-derived identity, defense-in-depth authorization, and private row mapping are coherent. But labels behavior is dispersed across many architectural roots, simple fixed-provider CRUD gains a repository port and one use-case wrapper per operation, and use-cases/shared/errors is a generic shared bucket.
